purpose: Constituents want to see you in person. Hear them out at the town hall, then open your door for office hours.
Lobbyists have asked for your time, and reporters will catch you on the way out. Listen without promising too much.
A listening tour: a town hall, a lobbyist, and a study session. Learn the issues before you have to vote on them.

description: Hearing at the Committee on the Environment
purpose: The Committee on the Environment holds a hearing. Line up your party first, face the press, then make your case to the committee.
A full round of media: a press conference, a TV debate and an ambush or two. Keep your tone steady from start to finish.

description: Providing the Party Agricultural Policy Support
purpose: The party needs help with its agricultural policy. Work the caucus, the lobbyists, and the committee, then carry it on the floor.

description: Providing the Party Infrastructure Policy Support
purpose: The party's infrastructure plan needs a champion. Study it, sell it on TV and in committee, and defend it on the floor.

description: Fighting on the Floor for the Party
purpose: Three floor debates, with reporters in between. The party is counting on you to hold the line in the chamber.
Colleagues are away, and you are filling their seats on several committees. Each one asks different questions.

description: Advancing a Bill to Protect Hometown Markets
purpose: Hometown markets want protection. Build support at home, then take the idea through committee and onto the floor.
Student organizers want a hearing. Meet them in the office, then at a town hall, and study what they are asking for.
A tour of the district's families. Their worries lead to two committees: the environment and construction.
Local artisans need a friend in the Assembly. Hear their lobby, then argue their case on the floor and in two committees.
The daily commute is getting worse. Take the complaints from your office to the committees and then to the floor.
The party's traditionalist wing is wary of you. Win them over in caucus, on TV, and in the Cabinet's own committee.
The reform caucus wants you on its side. Expect cameras, three committees, and a floor debate.
Younger voters could become a coalition. Meet them at home, carry their concerns through committee, and face the press.

description: Uniting Main Street and Transit Riders
purpose: Shop owners and transit riders want different things. Find the deal that serves both, from the lobby to the floor.

description: Bridging Old Guard and New Wave
purpose: The party's old guard and its new wave are pulling apart. Bridge them across a long run of committees and a floor debate.
Young people and labor could stand together. Study the case, win the party bodies, then the floor.
Neighborhood families want a compact with the Assembly. Build it from the town hall up through committee to the floor.
Small businesses want a coalition behind them. Argue for them on the floor, in committee, and on TV.
A big push for metro infrastructure. Expect lobbyists, two floor debates, and the party's steering committee.
The party's old order wants you to defend it. Expect the Cabinet, foreign affairs, war, and two floor debates.
The reform wave is rising, and the cameras are on you. Ride it through the press, four committees, and the floor.
Practice in coalition building: an office visitor, a town hall, and a lobbyist, each wanting something different.
Rural youth are leaving. Listen in the office, study the problem, and take it to the agriculture and environment committees.
Your Kōenkai family expects you to deliver. Show up at home, then in committee, in the party, and on the floor.
A main street infrastructure bill needs votes. Work the lobby, three committees, and the Cabinet, and keep the press calm.
A grand bargain across the party and the Cabinet. Every room wants something; the floor decides whether it holds.

Your constituents have called a town hall. Answer their questions honestly.
The party's steering committee wants a word about your recent record.

description: A Quiet Word with a Lobbyist
purpose: A lobbyist would like a quiet word. Listen carefully to what is being offered.
Your door is open. Visitors from the district are lining up.
A local festival, and a chance to be seen. Your neighbors will remember who came.
A few reporters have gathered outside. Keep it short and on message.

description: A Town Hall on Local Issues
purpose: A town hall on local issues. Expect questions about roads, clinics, and prices.
An evening of policy study. Learn the details before someone tests you on them.
A late TV interview. Keep your composure until the very end.
The autumn harvest festival. The farming towns are watching who turns up.
The winter snow festival. A cold night, a big crowd, and a lot of hands to shake.
A walk around the district. Talk to whoever stops you.
A community clinic day. Hear from patients and staff about what is missing.
A school visit. The students' questions will be harder than they look.
A stall at the farmers' market. Talk prices with the growers and the shoppers.
A radio debate. Without pictures, every word has to carry.
The morning call-in show. Anyone can call in, so expect anything.

description: A Fisheries Meeting at the Harbor
purpose: Fishers have called a meeting at the harbor. They want to know whose side you are on.
Students have invited you to a campus Q&A. Be ready for sharp questions.
A ward-by-ward walk with the local leaders, and a conversation for each corner.
A tour of the whole district. Everyone you pass will be sizing you up.
A big regional festival draws people from several towns. Be seen, and stay for the speeches.
The great festival of the year. The shrine, the towns, and the press will all be there.
A long open day at your office, and a longer line at the door.
The doors are open to everyone for a day, and the town leaders have been invited to watch.
A health fair with the clinic, the care workers, and the families who rely on them.
A forum on local care, with hospital staff, patients, and caregivers on one stage.
An education forum with teachers, parents, and students, all of whom have opinions.
A graduation ceremony, and a speech the families will quote for years.
A trade fair where local makers and buyers meet. Listen for what they cannot get done.
A large export expo with growers, makers, and buyers from beyond the district.
The party's candidate selection committee wants to hear your case before it decides.
